patches.title: Use libc for the standalone C minterm generator
patches.reason: Unused engine configuration headers prevent a standalone HOST build; preserve algorithm.

patches.title: Resolve generated includes through the build include path
patches.reason: Quoted includes prefer stale snapshot siblings over build/generated; the generated include directory must precede upstream.

patches.title: Recognize compiler AArch64 and select the explicit portable host boundary
patches.reason: Clang/GCC AArch64 is not recognized by WinUAE 6030; portable profile must not inherit Win32 services or calling-convention macros.

patches.title: Check portable allocation sizes before libc
patches.reason: Prevent wrapped array sizes and uae_u32 bank guard addition; retain libc ownership and the existing bank mapping.

patches.title: Select the closed portable zfile backend and disable implicit format/history probing
patches.reason: zfile.cpp mixes host filesystem, archives and RAM streams. Portable profile retains the pinned API/layout and compiles only bounded guest I/O; legacy backend remains unchanged for other targets.

patches.title: Format SHA1 hex bytes without TCHAR printf
patches.reason: Write exactly two uppercase hex digits per digest byte, retaining the final terminator; permits the full CRC/SHA unit in the portable profile without a variadic Windows alias. Algorithms unchanged.

patches.title: Exclude host display and clock waits from portable event dispatch
patches.reason: Frontend pacing must not run CPU while chipset time is stopped. Retain original event tables, handlers, cycle carry and countdown; custom pacing and frame return remain separate gates.
patches.test: BUILD01/HOST01; tests.host.test_events; T07 frame gate remains pending

patches.title: Declare passive fpdata scalar when FPU emulation is disabled
patches.reason: fpdata and fpp.h declarations exist unconditionally but fptype did not. Retain FPUEMU guards for regstruct storage and operations; no FPU implementation or callbacks added.

patches.title: Guard CPU common helpers with their backend features
patches.reason: Match CE020/CE030 prefetch guards and exclude FPU/MMU-dependent operations and frames when those backends are disabled; retain 68000 algorithms and passive control register storage.

patches.title: Expose DMA source tags independently of debugger support
patches.reason: Blitter memory writes pass access-source constants even when debug hooks are disabled. Move unchanged passive definitions outside DEBUGGER; retain all implementation guards.

patches.title: Compile CIA with portable limits and excluded host features
patches.reason: Exclude wall-clock TOD_HACK only in P6; retain emulated TOD. Use standard INT_MAX, match evt_t diagnostic width, and keep ReadCIAA parallel branch syntactically valid without PARALLEL_PORT.

patches.title: Read RTC calendar from emulated scheduler time
patches.reason: Replace CIA reads/battery writer and RTC null-tm fallback with explicit epoch/cycle clock; preserve chips and non-portable paths. Errors latch for bridge and never provide a successful default date.

patches.title: Keep CPU IRQ on the sole emulation thread
patches.reason: P6 owner-thread contract: retain synchronous IRQ branch; guard threaded and statusline includes and UI clear. No fake main-thread test or semaphore backend. ADR0002.
patches.test: tests.host.test_cpu_irq; HOST01/GEN01; CPU full compilation remains T06b2p

patches.title: Compile A500 CPU selection without unavailable families
patches.reason: Keep CE68000 assignments/run loop, one profile dispatch cell, common trace/prefetch. Exclude other-model cache helpers only in P6; debugger-disabled disassembly reports unavailable. ADR0003; remaining MMU/FPU callers still need link closure.
patches.test: tests.host.test_cpu_prefetch; BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01; full machine link remains T06b2r/T06c

patches.title: Exclude absent MMU/FPU CPU backends from A500
patches.reason: Guard backend callers and other-model cache/exception helpers, retaining A500 SR, bus-error signaling and non-MMU reset. No fake backend providers; ADR0003 configuration precondition remains.

patches.title: Keep CPU dump safe with debugger disabled
patches.reason: Guard unavailable prefetch decoding and disassembly walk: avoid uninitialized opcode, infinite prevpc loop and misleading Next PC output. Registers, latch and unsupported diagnostic remain.
patches.test: tests.host.test_cpu_prefetch with Werror=uninitialized and real dump execution; BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01

patches.title: Retain A500 device lifecycle without excluded host services
patches.reason: Preserve upstream registry and A500 hardware ordering; exclude host network/CD/MCU/UI/NATMEM/accelerator hooks. No provider stubs; ADR0004 reviews 16th touched upstream file and validated-config precondition.
patches.test: tests.host.test_devices; real lifecycle order and full-object import allowlist; BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01

patches.title: Keep mode0 CIA keyboard without MCU backends
patches.reason: Guard only MCU dispatch/callers in P6, preserving CIA software keyboard serial/handshake/resetwarning paths. Positive keyboard modes require rejection at public config gate; no MCU stubs.

patches.title: Exclude host sample ripping from portable Paula
patches.reason: WAV export and host paths are outside A500 deterministic output; keep synthesis and DMA unchanged. ADR0004 reviews audio.cpp as touched file17.

patches.title: Use defined multiplication for signed Paula amplitude scaling
patches.reason: Left shifts of negative PCM/sinc amplitudes are undefined in C++17. Multiplication preserves scale and fits the validated Paula sample/volume ranges; no changed rounding, clipping or timing.
patches.test: tests.host.test_pcm with audio_scale_probe; O0/O2 ASan/UBSan; BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01

patches.title: Compile SoftFloat with consistent linkage and case-exact includes
patches.reason: Audio tangent needs integer SoftFloat without FPU. Preserve arithmetic and notices; external inline float_raise matches its prior declaration and all callers include its definition.

patches.title: Configure Paula independently of host pacing and backend negotiation
patches.reason: Validate before arithmetic/live preferences, stop on backend failure without produce_sound fallback, and retain the physical clock established by init_sound. Filters and interpolation unchanged; custom video pacing remains separate.

patches.title: Expose shared halt and reset requests independently of CPUEMU_0
patches.reason: A500 CPUEMU_13 calls these helpers but their definitions were nested inside CPUEMU_0. Close and reopen that guard only around shared functions; retain MMU and opcode-debug selection.

patches.title: Keep Paula running while the CPU is halted
patches.reason: audio_deactivate clears Paula state and phase although haltloop still advances chipset time. P6 retains hardware state and PCM delivery; frontend stop/pause must not masquerade as a device reset.

patches.title: Keep custom field and Paula clocks independent of host pacing
patches.reason: Monitor refresh and turbo must not alter CIA/TOD field rate or Paula clock; preserve nominal field selection and raster geometry.

patches.title: Compile shared OCS color registers without AGA storage
patches.reason: Retain OCS writes and color lookup while guarding optional AGA arrays. Preserve PRNG consumption in reset.

patches.title: Exclude inactive custom host includes and callers
patches.reason: Threads are unused here; serial and special monitor calls require their feature. Format portable diagnostics within the real buffer and deliver them as text.

patches.title: Guard optional BSDSOCKET IRQ and CD32 TOD callers
patches.reason: Excluded devices must not remain link requirements of A500 custom IRQ and CIA sync. Keep A500 pulse generation and IRQ order unchanged.

patches.title: Keep HSync hardware work outside host waits
patches.reason: P6 advances hardware only by emulated cycles; remove per-line host wait and pull-audio policy while preserving CIA, input, IRQ, copper and reset ordering.

patches.title: Separate custom VSync buffer work from host presentation and clock
patches.reason: Keep Denise redraw/drain and hardware housekeeping; host wait/GPU/event pump/FPS must not drive portable frame advancement. Retire clear requests at the existing interlace cadence.

patches.title: Disable alternate Kickstart paths in portable memory loader
patches.reason: Preserve read_rom_name and its result; do not try host defaults or filename guesses after failure. ROM validation/fallback lifecycle remain separate gates.

patches.title: Expose ROM load failure and reject CPU entry without AROS fallback
patches.reason: Failed firmware load must remain causal state, not a diagnostic or implicit AROS substitution. Guard CPU before reset vectors; public firmware validation and bridge error propagation remain required.

patches.title: Reject short ROM reads and bad checksums without repair
patches.reason: P6 must reject truncated/corrupt payloads before CPU entry; checksum arithmetic must be unsigned (UBSan reproducer T06b2bc).

patches.title: Normalize explicit ROM assets with explicit keys and checked publication
patches.reason: Do not resolve alternate ROM/key paths or publish failed decode/normalization. Preserve local transforms and exact ownership.

patches.title: Validate complete A500 main firmware envelope before patching
patches.reason: Reject suffixes, malformed structures and unsupported executable/extended formats without adapting machine requirements.

patches.title: Format portable ROM names and reject excluded Arcadia configuration
patches.reason: Keep metadata display without a general TCHAR formatter; exclude Arcadia scanner and host-derived device filenames in the A500 profile.

patches.title: Select existing synchronous Denise dispatch without worker lifecycle
patches.reason: One emulation owner must execute RGA in caller order; exclude host thread/semaphore queue lifecycle and Windows-only statusline declaration.

patches.title: Compile OCS/ECS renderer with AGA and debugger disabled
patches.reason: Exclude disabled hardware decoders, generated AGA dispatch and unused host HUD; preserve OCS/ECS color, HAM and pixel implementations.

patches.title: Separate desktop launcher from engine globals and use explicit PRNG seed
patches.reason: P6 owns its public lifecycle and seed; do not compile desktop entrypoints or host-time fallback. Use actual board-array fields in disabled-autoconfig preference cleanup.

patches.title: Compile A500 expansion with explicit device catalog and portable names
patches.reason: Keep real card parsing/metadata and format only numeric device suffix with a bounded temporary; no broad formatting aliases or device stubs. Exclude unsupported A500 device catalog/helpers and FILESYS hooks; range-check indexed ROM-device lookup against the actual catalog.

patches.title: Clear each Fast and Z3 RAM board when applying base preset
patches.reason: The loop repeatedly clears slot0, retaining earlier configuration in all remaining slots. Index both arrays as the loop intends.
patches.test: BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01; tests.host.test_cfgfile_preset; dirty-board reproducer versus pristine

patches.title: Separate desktop configuration from library presets
patches.reason: The fixed P6 profile uses explicit validated configuration, not legacy host parser/exporter/CLI or implicit export cache. Preserve real prefs and diagnostics with portable varargs formatting.

patches.title: Exclude remaining desktop config cleanup and export callers
patches.reason: P6 has neither the private desktop parameter list nor configuration exporter after 0042. Remove their lifecycle calls, retaining actual hardware cleanup and preference fixups.
patches.test: BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01; tests.host.test_devices, tests.host.test_main_source; preprocessed dependency audit

patches.title: Keep shared state support without desktop slots or CD export
patches.reason: P6 uses frontend-neutral state APIs; legacy quick-slot paths and CD are excluded. Preserve core state helpers and bound the version header formatter.

patches.title: Match state diagnostic formats to actual integer types
patches.reason: size_t, uae_u32 and pointer differences require their own printf formats; long or unsigned int are not interchangeable on LP64/LLP64.

patches.title: Open explicit read-only disk assets without desktop path resolution
patches.reason: M1 media come from the bounded blob store. Keep ownership and CRC failures causal; never open host paths or accept ROM/key assets as floppy media.

patches.title: Exclude host-clock, overlay, catalogue and filesystem services from read-only floppy media
patches.reason: M1 floppies are immutable blob assets. ADF creation stamps the host clock, save-image overlays and write-protect toggling use host paths/chmod/unlink, the bootblock catalogue reads plugin XML, and next/previous disk probes host names. Each feature is excluded with its callers; executable content is rejected at the asset boundary instead of being converted with a host date. No success stubs.

patches.title: Keep logical input devices; exclude textual configuration, macros and desktop actions
patches.reason: The bridge feeds normalized keys and ports through internal setters (docs/02-contracts). Configuration text readers/writers, custom-event macros (ShellExecute, cfgfile parser), joystick-port custom text and HID-name scanning belong to excluded desktop configuration. RTG, debugger and mixer-volume actions, and the wall-clock auto-switch, are guarded. No success stubs; device-to-port assignment stays for T10.

patches.title: Drop CD32, parallel-port SCSI, input-recording and clock-file references from the A500 CIA
patches.reason: The link-closure gate (T06b2ce) showed cia.o still naming hardware and host services the A500 profile does not have: Akiko audio mute, parallel-port SCSI adapters, input-record debugging and battery-clock files resolved through the host filesystem. Each branch is excluded with its callers; the parallel port keeps its joystick/printer lines. Clock RAM persistence is not offered in M1 and the public config must reject rtcfile.

patches.title: Exclude input recording, accelerator boards, host memory protection and the trap area from the CPU core
patches.reason: The link-closure gate showed newcpu still naming excluded features: input record/playback hooks, cpuboard reset/fc hooks, JIT-only memory barriers and ROM protection, the UAE trap area and the debugger's real-bank lookup. Each is guarded at its caller; get_mem_bank_real (defined only in the debugger) becomes get_mem_bank, identical without memwatch. The MOVES function-code wrappers stay because cpuemu_13 uses them. Public config must reject cpuboard_type, inprecfile, uaeboard and JIT.

patches.title: Exclude accelerator, Gayle/Gary, trap-area and ROM-protection hooks from the memory map
patches.reason: memory.o still referenced cpuboard hooks, the A600/A1200/A3000 Gayle and mbres banks, Gary timeout flags (only written by those banks, hence constant zero), host ROM page protection, the UAE boot ROM/trap area and the debugger-only get_mem_bank_real. Guarded at the callers; ordinary A500 bank mapping and Gary non-range logic stay. Public config must normalize cs_ide to 0 (upstream sets -1 for generic configs, which maps Gayle), and reject cs_pcmcia, cs_fatgaryrev/cs_ramseyrev >= 0, cpuboard_type, uaeboard, cachesize and filesystem/RTG/SCSI options.

patches.title: Exclude input record/playback, trap-driven mousehack and cartridge descrambling from input, disk, state and ROM code
patches.reason: inputdevice, disk and savestate still called the input-recording API; savestate_capture only runs under input recording (it returns when input_record is off) so it and its callers are guarded; the magic mouse reads RTG/trap context through uaelib traps; Nordic Power/X-Power cartridge images need descrambling. Guarded at the callers, upstream text kept. A scrambled cartridge image now fails its CRC check; public config must reject inprecfile, state capture/rewind (statecapture*), uaeboard, input_tablet and ROMTYPE_ALL_CART, and the bridge must not expose AKS_STATECAPTURE.

patches.title: Exclude accelerator, RTG, directory-unit, UAE boot ROM and desktop-target hooks from configuration and expansion
patches.reason: main, expansion and cfgfile still called cpuboard sizing/autoconfig, graphics-board limits, directory-unit checks, the SCSI default and the desktop target hooks; filesys_bank showed as unresolved because its definition sits under FILESYS while two exported UAE-board helpers referenced it outside that block; need_uae_boot_rom depended on the traps area (rtarea_base, zero when it is not built) and now returns no boot ROM. Guarded at the callers, upstream text kept. Dropping target_default_options changes host-side defaults the core never reads (sampler card, gfx api). Public config must reject cpuboard_type, rtg memory/type/initial_active/monitor_id, z3 chip/fast memory, non-default cdslots, scsi, directory mounts, uaeboard and cachesize.

patches.title: Let gencpu emit only the CPU models named on its command line
patches.reason: gencpu writes cpustbl.cpp and one handler file per CPU model in a fixed loop, so the generated table names about 11859 handlers of models the profile never compiles (only CPUEMU_13 is built) and the link cannot resolve them. Generated output must not be edited, so the generator gets an optional list of model numbers, validated before any file is created; without arguments it behaves exactly as upstream (tested byte for byte). The recipe asks for models 13 and 14 (68000 cycle-exact handlers and their table).

patches.title: Exclude the legacy .uss file machinery of savestate.cpp until the native serializer
patches.reason: savestate.cpp writes and reads WinUAE .uss files: it calls every per-device save_*/restore_*, resolves host paths, compresses with zlib, saves screenshots and wav headers. The native serializer (T15) reuses the upstream per-device functions with in-memory I/O and its own envelope, so the file machinery is excluded rather than faked: save_state/restore_state and their helpers, the path and string savers, rewind and memorysave, and the save/restore/rewind branches of savestate_check (left as return false, since serving them without a restorer would leave savestate_state stuck). The state variables and byte primitives other units use stay. SAVESTATE is not defined in the profile, so the per-device functions do not exist yet.

patches.title: Exclude desktop actions, host paths, wall-clock and message-table services from the engine units
patches.reason: inputdevice, disk, rommgr, main, custom, newcpu, cfgfile and memory still called services that only a desktop host provides: AKS actions for GUI, screen, volume, RTG, video grab and quick save, the recent-file list and OSD text, host ROM directories and path comparison, the message-resource table, quit/restart hooks, wall-clock helpers and the .uss restore. Each is guarded at its caller. Emulator-internal AKS actions stay (reset, eject, port swap, input config, IRQ7, disk swapper, refresh, quit/restart, rewind). Firmware paths are logical ids compared exactly; ROM identification by file name (which accepted unhashed content) is excluded, so identity rests on CRC/SHA-1; the missing-ROM text is a fixed English string on the diagnostics queue. setsystime is excluded (a no-op with tod_hack = 0, which the public config must require); tablet/lightpen and edge/switch helpers that need desktop coordinates are excluded.

patches.title: Exclude the on-screen keyboard, paste, the host pause flag and the host key-swap hack
patches.reason: The on-screen keyboard is a desktop overlay (osk_setup, target_osk_control, target_osd_keyboard) and paste reads the host clipboard: both are AKS actions the bridge cannot raise. keybuf.cpp read two host-owned variables: pause_emulation (the desktop pause; the bridge decides when frames run) and key_swap_hack (a Windows keyboard-layout correction; the bridge already sends Amiga raw scancodes). Guarded at the callers instead of defining constant variables.

patches.title: Call the graphics-board refresh only when graphics boards are built
patches.reason: full_redraw_all called gfxboard_refresh under picasso_on, which is never set in the A500 profile (no graphics boards); the definition lives in the excluded board code, so the reference only ever served the link. PICASSO96 is the feature macro upstream already uses for the surrounding board code and it stays undefined, so the guard is an upstream candidate and is not tied to the profile flag.

patches.title: Leave the GUI observation state to the portable layer
patches.reason: main.cpp defines no_gui, quit_to_gui and gui_data with the values of the desktop launcher, and ports/portable/gui.cpp defines the same three with the headless values (no_gui = true) that the observational GUI services use; linking both fails with duplicate symbols. The port owns the state, so the definitions in main.cpp are guarded.
patches.test: BUILD01/HOST01/GEN01; tests.codegen.test_engine_imports (link without duplicate symbols); tests.host.test_diagnostics

patches.title: Return from the CPU loop at every rendered video unit
patches.reason: The CPU loop must hand control back to the bridge at a video boundary and resume there without a second scheduler, stack switch or thread: vsync_display_render raises SPCFLAG_UNIT_END, do_specialties/haltloop/CPUINRESET poll it and m68k_go becomes the resumable m68k_go_unit.

patches.title: Defined pointer arithmetic and shifts in the Denise line drawing
patches.reason: The first video unit runs the line drawing before any line buffer is locked; adding the low-res shift to NULL and shifting the negative pixel-count sentinel are undefined behaviour that ASan/UBSan builds abort on. Both rewrites keep the values of valid buffers.

patches.title: Test-only hook at each video boundary
patches.reason: STEP01 compares N resumed calls with the same engine advancing N units without returning; that needs an observer and a way to swallow boundaries at every place where the boundary is decided (the instruction tail and both wait loops). The blocks exist only when P6_UNIT_TRACE is defined, which no profile or release build does.

patches.title: Free space of the keyboard ring
patches.reason: A full ring drops the new code, which leaves a key stuck in the guest. The bridge needs the free space to send an edge only when it fits and to retry the rest at the next unit.

patches.title: Report each boundary once in trace builds
patches.reason: In a CPU held in reset the wait loop and the tail of do_specialties both see the boundary; the observer of a trace build must report it once or the N-calls comparison counts it twice.

patches.title: Record the guest's reads of input registers
patches.reason: P6_FRAME_LAG must follow what the emulated CPU reads (JOYxDAT, POTxDAT, POTGOR, CIA-A PRA and SDR), not the frontend's poll. A write-only bit mask that the bridge clears at the start of a unit and reads at the end records it without a callback from inside the engine.

patches.title: Clear the engine's key table for a reset requested through the API
patches.reason: p6_reset restarts the machine at a boundary without the Ctrl-Amiga-Amiga path, which is the only code that cleared the engine's key table and the reset-chord state; a key held across the reset would stay down for the engine and a half-run chord would fire later.

patches.title: Forget the last reported boundary at a reset head
patches.reason: The STEP01 observer ignores a boundary at the same cycle count as the previous one (the wait loop of a CPU in reset and the tail of do_specialties can both see it). A reset restarts the counter, so the boundary of the unit after two consecutive resets fell on the same count and was not reported. Trace builds only.

patches.title: Start every session with the floppy head on track 0
patches.reason: floppy[].cyl lives in a static array that DISK_init never touched, so a second p6_load in the same process began with the head where the previous session left it and did not match a clean process. A reset keeps the head, as a real drive does; only a load starts over.

patches.title: Put the pot port state back at every reset
patches.reason: potgo_value, pot_cap, pot_dat and pot_dat_act are chip state that inputdevice_reset never touched: only a cold process has them at zero, so POTGOR and the pot counters of a new load depended on what the previous session did with POTGO.

patches.title: Reset the secondary event scheduler with the events
patches.reason: event2idx (where MISC_handler starts its round) and the re-entry counters are static and survived clear_events, so the order of two secondary events due at the same instant, and the slot the next one takes, depended on the previous session.

patches.title: Forget the instant of the last CIA service at a reset
patches.reason: cia_now_evt is compared with regs.ipl_evt when an interrupt is recognised, but the cycle counter restarts at a reset and nothing put it back, so the IPL timing of the first CIA interrupts of a load depended on the previous session; a clean process has both at zero.

patches.title: Give each preference set its own device names
patches.reason: copy_prefs and copy_inputdevice_prefs memcpy the input device settings, so the name and configname strings that matchdevices had allocated for the destination were dropped without being freed on every load (and the destination then shared the source's strings). Each set now frees what it owns before the copy and duplicates the source's strings after it.

patches.title: Tell the bridge when the cycle counter starts over
patches.reason: The reset head restarts the engine's cycle counter for every kind of reset, but only a reset asked for through p6_reset told the bridge: the emulated clock kept the old cycle and faulted the image on its next read, and the caller's tick count dropped the part of the unit before the restart, after a keyboard reset chord. A function pointer, set by the bridge while an image is loaded, is called from the one place where the counter restarts.

patches.title: The first CIA frame of a load is a process's first frame
patches.reason: cia_cycle_accurate is computed at the end of each frame and is false in a process that has not finished one; a reload kept the last session's true, so the keyboard interrupts of unit 1 came later than in a clean process and left a different PC on the stack. The bridge calls this at load.

patches.title: An input session leaves no counters behind
patches.reason: A session that moved the mouse left mouse_x/y, mouse_frame_x/y, the pending axes and the frame counters of getvelocity in the data segment; the next load started JOY0DAT from them ($0A10 instead of $0101 for input_all after a script that moves the mouse). A load now puts them back to the value of a process that has seen no input; a reset inside a session keeps them, as the hardware does.

patches.title: The native state can read and write the live random generator
patches.reason: xorshiftstate is a file static of main.cpp that decides the floppy jitter, the start-up delay and the chip-colour power-up; p6_rng_get/p6_rng_set expose only the generator state (randseed is the configuration's seed, bound by config_hash). Pure accessors.

patches.title: The native state can check that the CPU is at a unit boundary
patches.reason: p6_cpu_boundary names the first reason an instruction boundary is not a state: the CPU loop not started, an exception in flight, a register or mode only a 68010 has, a flag the profile never leaves pending, or a file-local counter off its boundary value. These are file statics of newcpu.cpp that a state cannot see; the function only reads them and is added at the end of the file, so m68k_go_unit is untouched.

patches.title: The native state can read and write the secondary scheduler's file-local state, and a load puts its cursor back
patches.reason: event2idx (which of two events due together runs first) and the allocation cursor of event2_newevent_xx (a function-local static, promoted to a file static under the same value) decide the order of events, and cycles_to_add_remain is the sub-CYCLE_UNIT remainder of do_cycles_slow; none can be seen from outside. p6_events_get/p6_events_set read them and, for a restore, write them and leave the re-entry counters of MISC_handler at zero. clear_events() also puts the cursor back to ev2_misc, next to the index patch 0070 already reset: a reload kept the cursor of the last session, so the same events landed in other slots than in a clean process and the slot decides ties (found by the extended scheduler digest of the state probe). A clean process starts at ev2_misc and its first reset head calls clear_events, so nothing changes there.

patches.title: The native state can read the half-CCK remainder of the CPU and name the static event handlers
patches.reason: extra_cycle (a file static) is the half-CCK remainder of the cycle-exact CPU, consumed by the next chip-bus access, and three secondary-event handlers (event_doint_delay_do_intreq, event_doint_delay_do_intena, fakehsync_handler) are static, so a state cannot name them; p6_custom_extra_cycle_get/set and p6_custom_event2_handler expose them. Pure accessors.

patches.title: The native state can name the floppy motor-off delay handler
patches.reason: motordelay_func is the static handler of the secondary event that ends the motor-off delay; a state names events by ids of its own, so the handler is exported through p6_disk_motordelay_handler. Pure accessor.

patches.title: The native state can read and write the MSM6242B's control registers
patches.reason: The control registers D, E and F of the clock chip are a file-static struct of cia.cpp, so a state cannot see them; p6_rtc_msm_get/set copy them out and in and nothing else. They are the only part of the clock the CPU can change and that is not in the bridge's civil clock (ports/portable/rtc_time.cpp).

patches.title: The native state can read and write the two CIAs and what cia.cpp keeps beside them
patches.reason: cia.cpp keeps both CIAs, the keyboard handshake, the E-clock phase and the LED in file statics, so a state cannot see them. p6_cia_get/set and p6_cia_misc_get/set copy fields into and out of plain structs (ports/portable/p6_state_access.h) and call nothing: CIA_update, CIA_calctimers, CIA_check_ICR and compute_passed_time change the live CIA or schedule events that the scheduler's chunk owns. p6_cia_overlay_rebuild makes the ROM-at-zero map again from PRA and DDRA, and p6_cia_boundary refuses a CIA that fields alone cannot describe.

patches.title: A load starts with the power LED as a clean process has it
patches.reason: led_old_brightness (a static of cia.cpp) and gui_data.powerled/powerled_brightness (ports/portable/gui.cpp) are not put back by CIA_reset or p6_gui_reset. After a session that ended with the LED lit, a reload began with powerled set, and led_filter_audio() in the reset head read it, so the audio filter of the first unit differed from a clean process until the first led_vsync. p6_cia_session_begin now zeroes the three, the value of a clean process; a reset inside a session keeps them, as the hardware keeps the LED.

patches.title: The native state can read and write the keyboard ring
patches.reason: The ring of key codes that feeds the CIA serial line is a pair of indexes and an array in file statics of keybuf.cpp. p6_keybuf_get/set copy it as a list from the oldest code to the newest, so a state does not depend on where in the array it starts, and p6_keybuf_boundary refuses text being typed into it, a release held back or one to swallow. Nothing is called: record_key would add to the ring.

patches.title: The native state can read and write the input of the two gameports, the pot lines and the host's edge memory
patches.reason: inputdevice.cpp keeps the quadrature counters, the pending motion, the direction memory, the pot lines and the key table of the engine, and the host's edge memory (joysticks2, mice2), in file statics. p6_input_get/set copy them into and out of plain structs and call no setter: inputdevice_do_keyboard would put keys in the ring, resetinput and inputdevice_updateconfig erase the configuration, and handle_input_event would run events again. p6_input_boundary refuses what the profile does not have and what the fields do not hold.

patches.title: The save_*/restore_*/*_finish bodies of disk, chipset and blitter compile with P6_STATE_BODIES, without SAVESTATE
patches.reason: disk.cpp, custom.cpp and blitter.cpp keep the serializers of the floppy, the chipset registers, the copper and RGA slots, the sprites and the blitter under SAVESTATE, together with sites that change behaviour. The native state (bridge/state_upstream.cpp) reuses those bodies, so the guard of the functions alone also admits P6_STATE_BODIES; AGAC, CHPX, CHPD and CYCS, custom_prepare_savestate and the quit-state site stay under SAVESTATE alone. Defining SAVESTATE would also pull the ASF container and the m68k_go, savestate_init and quitstatefile sites, and nothing here does.

patches.title: save_disk and restore_disk write and read the drive without an image path and never insert or eject a medium
patches.reason: The upstream floppy body saves the image name and, for a full path, the host's idea of it, and restores by inserting the file again with drive_insert (zfile_exists, the delayed-change fake). save_path and restore_path do not exist in the portable build, the medium of a native state is the one the envelope's media manifest names, and restore_disk reads a flag that save_disk only writes when it was asked for a path. The portable body is 24 bytes: the CRC drive_insert measured replaces getadfcrc, which read the whole image through the zfile on every save, and the flag is always written, as zero.

patches.title: save_custom and restore_custom compile without AGA, keep to the six bitplane pointers of the profile, and a save does not store DMACONR into dmacon
patches.reason: The chipset body names the 32-bit AGA colour registers and writes eight BPLxPT: without AGA color_entry has no color_regs_aga and bplpt has MAX_PLANES (6) entries, so the body does not compile and restore would write two pointers past the array (the slot pipeline names BPL7PT and BPL8PT the same way). BPL7PT and BPL8PT travel as zero and are not stored. save_custom also stores the derived busy and zero bits of DMACONR into the live dmacon, and a state save must not change the machine, so the register image is computed without the store. The pot poll mask and the joystick reads of the same function are handled by the caller (STATE_DOSAVE, the mask put back).

patches.title: The Denise bitplane body reads and writes the six BPLxDAT of the profile, not eight
patches.reason: save_custom_bpl, restore_custom_bpl, save_custom_bpl_dat and restore_custom_bpl_dat index bplxdat, bplxdat2, bplxdat3 and their 64-bit twins for eight planes, and without AGA the arrays have MAX_PLANES (6) entries: a save would read the neighbouring statics, whose bytes depend on the layout of the build, and a restore would write over them. The planes the profile does not have travel as zero, so the body keeps its 292 bytes, and are not stored.

patches.title: restore_custom applies on a live machine: no audio_reset, no blitter_reset, no preference writes
patches.reason: restore_custom is a mini reset: it calls audio_reset (channels, filter state and pending PCM dropped), restore_blitter_start (blitter_reset) and writes chipset_mask and ntscmode into currprefs and changed_prefs. The native state applies the body on a running machine whose configuration is part of the identity: the bridge validates that the body names the configuration it has, and the patch removes the three effects that would otherwise discard live state or adapt the configuration to the body.

patches.title: restore_disk no longer writes the drive type or the number of floppies into the preferences
patches.reason: The portable restore_disk of patch 0087 still copied the type of the drive (dfxtype) and, for a disabled drive, nr_floppies into currprefs and changed_prefs, as upstream does to adapt the machine to a statefile. A native state never adapts the configuration: it is part of the identity, and the bridge refuses a DSKn body whose drive id or disabled bit is not the one of the configuration. With that check the writes would be no-ops, and without it they would be an adaptation, so they go.

patches.title: The CHSL body names the refresh, audio and disk pointers of an RGA slot
patches.reason: save_custom_slots stores each slot's pointer as the register getregfrompt maps it to, and restore_custom_slots maps it back with getptfromreg. Only the blitter, bitplane, sprite and copper pointers had a code: the pointers of the refresh and strobe slots (refptr) and of the audio and disk DMA slots came back as null, and handle_rga_out dereferences r->p for them, so a state taken with one of those slots in the pipeline crashed the first unit after a load. They get codes above the register file (0x200 refresh, 0x201-0x204 audio channels, 0x205 disk), and two accessors return the audio and disk pointers without audio_getpt's and disk_getpt's side effects, which a save may not have.

patches.title: restore_blitter_new keeps the old skip flags a type 2 body carries
patches.reason: A body of type 2 stores shifter_skip_b_old and shifter_skip_y_old and restore_blitter_new reads them into the variables, but the cycle-exact branch then overwrites both with the current skip flags, which blit_bltset has just derived from BLTCON0 and BLTCON1 and which do not say what the previous blit left. A state saved with the flags set came back with them cleared (and the reverse), so save, load, save did not give the same BLTX and BLIT bodies. Only a body older than type 2, which carries no flags, derives them.

patches.title: The beam, the frame phase and the DMA list of the line, as values
patches.reason: WinUAE's bodies throw the beam away (restore_custom reads VPOSR and VHPOSR and discards them) and keep the line history, the counters of the frame (display_hsync_counter, display_vsync_counter, maxvpos_display_vsync_next), prev_strobe (the strobe edge that raises the vertical blank: a restored machine had the reset value and raised a spurious one), dmal_shifter, dmal and dmal_next (the DMA list of the line in flight, which also paces the input's per-line tick) and the sync latches of Agnus in file statics no body names. p6_custom_beam_get and p6_custom_beam_set copy them as 61 32-bit words and derive only the line length (setmaxhpos). Without them a loaded machine keeps its own beam and a new image ends its first unit on another line and takes a vertical blank the original did not (DET02, T15f1).

patches.title: The Copper's waiting state and strobe, as values
patches.reason: WinUAE's CHSL keeps the Copper's ip and instruction words and puts its state back as stopped (or as the last cycle of a MOVE), so a Copper that was waiting for a beam position, skipping, or in the middle of a strobe comes back stopped and the interrupt it was going to raise never happens. p6_custom_copper_get and p6_custom_copper_set copy the rest of cop_state (state, state_prev, strobe_next, strobeip, vblankip, ignore_next, vcmp, hcmp, strobe, strobetype), the line flag copper_enabled_thisline and the time stamps strobe_cycles and copper_dma_change_cycle as 15 32-bit words, without running the Copper or recomputing the flag (DET02, T15f2).

patches.title: The fourth slot of the RGA pipeline in CHSL
patches.reason: rga_pipe has RGA_SLOT_TOTAL + 1 entries (custom_reset clears all four) and the three live ones are first+1..first+3, but save_custom_slots and restore_custom_slots walk only RGA_SLOT_TOTAL: with rga_slot_first_offset 0 a blit D write in flight sits in the fourth slot, is not saved, and a load keeps the live machine's (a restarted image ended a blit with BLTDPT 0x51728 instead of 0x60000 and left ~10 KiB unwritten). Both loops cover the whole pipeline; CHSL grows from 191 to 245 bytes (DET02, T15f3).

patches.title: Blitter phase state access
patches.reason: STATE02/DET02: a blit in flight under DMA contention comes back with its phase: blit_queued, blit_count_done, blt_change_cycles, the data path latches, the pending BLTCON/modulo flag and blit_dmacount/blit_cyclecount, which restore_blitter_new drops or derives. p6_blitter_phase_get/set copy them as 18 32-bit words without running the blitter (T15f3).

patches.title: Agnus values derived from the restored registers
patches.reason: STATE02/DET02: custom_reset's isrestore branch rebuilds what the engine derives from the registers (setup_fmodes: bplcon0_planes, bplcon0_planes_limit, bpl_sequence, curr_diagram, fetch unit, fmode_inuse; the sprite width; SPRxCTLPOS: vstart, vstop, dblscan of every sprite) and the bridge never runs custom_reset on a live machine, so an image that had not written the same registers itself (restarted before the load, or a new process) fetched its bitplanes from the planes of its reset and its CPU lost bus slots differently on the Kickstart keyboard handshake. p6_custom_rebuild_derived recomputes them from the registers without writing any, scheduling or running anything (T15f).

patches.title: Paula state that AUDn does not carry
patches.reason: STATE02/DET02: restore_audio puts back the registers of a channel and zeroes the rest, and restore_audio_finish sets last_cycles to the cycle of the load, so a restored machine started its resampler phase (next_sample_evtime) from zero, handed over 958 instead of 959 samples, lost the state of the output filters, the LED filter, the interpolation integrator, the DMA latches of every channel (pbufldl, dat_written, dat2, irqcheck, dmaenstore) and the period sentinel PERIOD_MAX - 1, and kept the ADKCON masks of the live machine. p6_audio_phase_get/set copy them as values without running Paula or scheduling anything (T15e).

patches.title: What Denise and the presentation keep outside every body: border colour, output pipeline, measured raster size
patches.reason: STATE02/DET02: three things a picture depends on are in no body and WinUAE's own load gets them from custom_reset/init_hz, which the bridge never runs on a live machine. (1) bordercolor and bordercolor_ecs_shres are derived from COLOR00 and BPLCON3, but restore_custom flushes its BPLCON writes (which recompute them) before docols rebuilds acolors, so a new image drew its first border black where the state's COLOR00 was red (p6_denise_rebuild_derived). (2) The four-pixel output pipeline dtbuf/dtgbuf feeds the first pixels of a line, and a machine that had not drawn the same lines put zero where the original put the border colour (p6_denise_pipe_get/set). (3) The raster size the engine measures and adopts after a few frames (current_linear_*, its candidate and countdown, the in/out geometry of the drawing buffer) was kept by the loading image or adopted units later with a blank picture, so the same program showed 576 lines where the original showed 574 (p6_frame_geometry_get/set). Values only; nothing runs or is scheduled (T15g).

patches.title: Floppy controller state that DSKn, DSDn and DISK do not carry
patches.reason: STATE02/DET02: save_floppy keeps only the low byte of disk_hpos (a machine that a CPU read of DSKBYTR had brought up to the middle of a line was brought up from the start of it after a load and read another word of the track), dsklen2 (one DSKLEN write or two start a transfer) is in no body, restore_disk zeroes dskchange_time (a delayed insert never lands) and no body carries the step limiter, the index decay, the wordsync edge flag, the motor-off latch or the geometry and bit counter of a drive with no buffered track (an empty drive that keeps spinning). p6_disk_phase_get/set copy them as values without running the drives or scheduling anything, and p6_disk_newname_set names the image a delayed insert is waiting for (T15d).

patches.title: Defined arithmetic for the position DISK_update is brought up to
patches.reason: FUZZ01: a state load runs restore_custom, whose DSKSYNC(-1, value) calls DISK_update(-1) (the register image is written without moving the drives); the engine then shifts the negative position left, which is undefined in C++17 (UBSan, left shift of negative value -1) in every load. Multiplication by 256 is the same value for every position the drives are brought up to and defines the -1 of a register restore.

patches.title: The vertical window lines, the refused raster mode and the rows of the picture come back with the state
patches.reason: T15j: a state saved, loaded and saved again differed from one saved without the load in the vertical window bit of DIWHIGH (plffirstline and plflastline are file statics that custom_reset leaves at 0 and 0 and restore_custom derives with calcvdiw); the first picture after a load was the history of the abandoned timeline or of a fresh machine whenever the engine draws no line in a unit (the pixel rows are engine state in practice); and a raster refused as larger than the presentation buffer (compute_framesync clamps the sizes afterwards, so GEOM looked like a mode that fits) drew pictures after the load that the original never handed over.

patches.title: The flags that say the beam registers were programmed come back with the state
patches.reason: T23b: on an ECS Agnus restore_custom sets programmed_register_accessed_h (SPRHSTRT, BPLHSTRT and the rest of the 1D0-1EE block) whatever the registers hold, so a machine that loaded a state ran check_hsyncs_programmed in every line, and its extra update_agnus_vb call at line 0 copied linear_vpos_visible into current_linear_vpos_visible a line late (288 against 287). The two flags are not derived from the registers; the BEAM body carries them (65 to 67 words).

patches.title: The drive-select latch of the floppy controller comes back with the state
patches.reason: T15k: DISK_select keeps the drive-select mask, the step line and the direction in file statics derived from the last write to CIA-B port B (prev_data); upstream rebuilds them with DISK_select_set from restore_cia_finish, which the native load does not run. A loaded machine had every drive deselected and the step line low, so the first port B write after the load did not step the drive the original stepped (nor draw the random shifter bits), and the generator and the head diverged during a DOS load. DSKX carries prev_data (40 to 41 words) and the apply calls DISK_select_set.

patches.title: Select and run the 68020 cycle-exact core (cpuemu_21) without FPU, MMU or data cache
patches.reason: T24a: the profile compiled only the 68000 CE family. The 68020 helpers (instruction cache, pipeline, delayed accesses, prefetch fill), the CE020 accessor set, the cputbls row, the interrupt-delay flag, the CE020 loop m68k_run_2ce, the 68020 exception branch (formats 0, 2 and, without MMU state, B) and the model switch of m68k_run/fill_prefetch are brought back; the 68030/68040 blocks stay out. External bus errors are not modelled without an MMU (upstream's do_access_or_bus_error returns in that case too).

patches.title: Accept a Kickstart whose CPU requirement the preset meets
patches.reason: T24b: patch 0035 refused every ROM with a CPU requirement in rommgr (cpu & 15). The A1200 Kickstart 3.1 (cpu = 1, 68EC020 minimum) is the firmware of the first 68020 machine; the loader now compares the ROM requirement with the CPU of the preset as upstream load_kickstart does (68030+ and the A4000 ROMs stay refused, a 68000 preset still refuses a 68EC020 ROM).

patches.title: State access for the 68020 and AGA: the instruction cache, the CE020 remainder, the AGA palette body and the fetch size
patches.reason: T24c: the native state of the A1200 needs what the 68020 keeps in file-local variables (caches020, the sub-CCK remainder of do_cycles_ce020), the AGA palette body (save_custom_agacolors/restore_custom_agacolors were only under SAVESTATE), the handler id of setup_fmodes_delayed, the size of a fetch that p6_custom_rebuild_derived left to setup_fmodes (which skips it once fmode_inuse equals FMODE) and a boundary check that no longer refuses the registers a 68020 has.

patches.title: State access for the Agnus-to-Denise ring cursors
patches.reason: T24c: DET02 on the A1200 (the program rewrites FMODE all the time) shows that the first pixels of a line depend on what the slots of rga_denise held from an earlier revolution, which the position of the write cursor selects; the slots are public but the cursors are file-local statics of custom.cpp.

patches.title: Disk images with a write overlay open read-write and report write protection from the pool
patches.reason: T27: the portable DISK_validate_filename opens every image rb and reports it write protected; a session that reserved a write overlay needs the medium opened over it (r+b, base never written) and the drive's /WPRO to follow how much room the overlay has left.

patches.title: A track the guest wrote that is not AmigaDOS is kept and read back
patches.reason: T27: with a plain ADF the portable build dropped a written track that does not decode into eleven sectors (convert_adf_to_ext2 is compiled out). The track the guest wrote is kept as raw MFM words in the write overlay and the drive builds the read from them, until the guest writes the track as AmigaDOS again.

patches.title: Autoconfig and the first Zorro II Fast RAM board while one is configured
patches.reason: T49: Fast RAM is a Zorro II autoconfig board, and the port compiled the autoconfig entry points out (AUTOCONFIG is not defined: it also brings the trap area, emulib and native-call hooks, none of which the profile has). The four sites that matter (expansion_map in memory_reset, expamem_reset at the end of custom_reset, board 0 kept by fixup_prefs, expansion_cleanup at leave) are enabled by P6_PORTABLE alone, and the first two only while fastmem[0].size is nonzero, so that a machine without Fast RAM keeps its E80000 window and every golden byte for byte. A cleaned-up bank forgets its size and address, so the next image allocates and configures its own.

patches.title: A Zorro II board is read and written at the address its guest gave it
patches.reason: T49: the accessors of a RAM bank subtract startaccessmask, which only the allocation sets, from the start the bank had then. The Fast RAM board is allocated when the image is loaded, before the guest chooses its base, so a board that fills the Zorro II space (8 MiB at 200000, where start & mask is 200000) was addressed a rotation away from its place: self consistent for the guest and wrong for a host that reads the region at an address. The map function sets the masks from the base it has just been given.

patches.title: State access for the autoconfig chain and the position of the Zorro II Fast RAM board
patches.reason: T49: a state taken while the guest is mid-way through the autoconfig chain (a card presented, a half-written base) or after the board has been given its base must put both back; ecard, chipdone, the base nibbles and expamem are file-local statics of expansion.cpp. Values only; the mapping of the board and of the E80000 window is rebuilt as expamem_next and expamem_map_fastcard leave them.

patches.title: Allocate the Zorro II Fast RAM board with the machine
patches.reason: T49: expansion_init is the WinUAE call that allocates the board, from virtualdevice_init, and it sat under AUTOCONFIG with the trap-area installers. With it the board exists when p6_load returns (its region, and the state bound, which depends on its size), and a reload with the same size finds a board to reuse instead of the one expansion_cleanup freed.

patches.title: A board is cleared without touching what is already zero
patches.reason: T49: expansion_clear (every hard reset, and the power-on of a load) memsets the Fast RAM board, and a board that was just allocated zeroed (calloc) had its pages dirtied by the zeros: a Waterbox snapshot carries every dirty page, so an 8 MiB board added 8 MiB to each snapshot (measured 10.2 MB to 18.7 MB on the A1200). Only the non-zero words are cleared, the result is the same.

patches.title: FPU 68881/68882 over SoftFloat only
patches.reason: FPUEMU turns on fpp.cpp; fpu_reset and fpu_modechange always use fp_init_softfloat (fpp_native and the x87 control word are not linked), the 68000 FPU hack of build_cpufunctbl is out and the F-line override of a 68020 leaves the coprocessor-1 opcodes to the FPU when fpu_model is set

patches.title: FPU without the 68030 MMU bookkeeping and the Windows x87 hook
patches.reason: fpp.cpp references mmu030_state/mmu030_data_buffer_out/mmu030_fmovem_store (cpummu030.cpp, MMUEMU) and od-win32's fpux_restore; neither exists in the profile, so the 68030 restartable-FMOVEM branch is compiled out and the x87 control word is never touched

patches.title: FPU FSAVE data accessors for the native state
patches.reason: fsave_data (condition/command word and exceptional operand of the last FPU exception) is file-local to fpp.cpp and an FSAVE after a trapped operation writes it into the frame; the CPU chunk carries it, so the bridge gets read/write accessors

patches.title: SoftFloat macro header include with the case of the file
patches.reason: fpp_softfloat.cpp and softfloat_decimal.cpp include softfloat-macros.h, which only resolves on a case-insensitive file system; the file is SOFTFLOAT-MACROS.H (patch 0021 did the same for softfloat.cpp), so the FPU builds on Linux

patches.title: FPU exceptions end the instruction of the CE020 handler
patches.reason: fp_exception_pending and FTRAPcc raise an exception without setting regs.fp_exception, so the generated cpuemu_21 handler goes on to refill the prefetch queue after the exception has set it up for the handler: the CPU then runs the handler's operands as opcodes (a taken FTRAPcc, or the instruction after a posted FPU exception, never reached its handler); setting fp_exception returns from the handler as TRAPcc does

patches.title: FMOD and FREM quotient through a uint64_t
patches.reason: uae_u64 is unsigned long long and SoftFloat's uint64_t is unsigned long on LP64 Linux, so floatx80_mod/floatx80_rem did not accept the quotient pointer there (macOS has both as unsigned long long); the FPU only built on the Darwin row

patches.title: The EXTER work queue of native2amiga is built under P6_NATIVE2AMIGA, not SUPPORT_THREADS
patches.reason: T29a: uae_ReplyMsg and its siblings are how a finished host-side request reaches the 68k (native2amiga_pending, drained by exter_int_helper at INT2). Upstream keys the queue on SUPPORT_THREADS, a name that stands for the Windows thread layer and is excluded from this profile. The queue itself only needs counting semaphores when one thread fills and drains it (ports/portable/threaddep/thread.h), so it stays under a macro of its own; the function pointer of uae_Signal_with_Func is cast for the queue's void* slot.

patches.title: uaehf.device serves a request in line, over flat images, without threads, SCSI or container formats
patches.reason: T29a: upstream starts one host thread per unit and queues every read and write to it; the instant the guest sees the reply then depends on the scheduler of the host. A block of an image in memory takes no emulated time, so BeginIO runs what the thread ran (hardfile_do_io, the ReplyMsg through native2amiga_pending) before it returns, and the finish reaches the guest at the next INT2. The unit has no thread (start_thread only records the base of the device), HD_SCSICMD answers IOERR_NOCMD (scsi.cpp is not built), and an image is a flat byte range read through hdf_open_target: no VHD, CHD, geometry .ini or host file system handler. hdf_close frees the generated RDB, which upstream frees only in the CHD branch. AdIDE scrambling (ide.cpp tables) is not recognized, and the version reader of the file system image of the generated RDB (atol) goes with it.

patches.title: Direct traps only: an extended trap or a hardware-trap thread stops the build with a reason
patches.reason: T29a: m68k_handle_trap runs a simple trap in line (handler(NULL), registers read from the CPU); only an extended trap (TRAPFLAG_EXTRA_STACK) and the hardware traps of uaeboard > 2 start threads. The profile selects neither, so the thread starts, joins and sleeps (init_traps, reset_traps, free_traps, the slot wait of alloc_host_main_trap_context) are removed and trap_HandleExtendedTrap reports and stops if some day one is registered.

patches.title: filesys.cpp for hard files: only UAE-controller hard files become units, bounded RDB parsing, no extra stack, no host date, no unbounded printf, no state bodies yet
patches.reason: T29a: the UAEFS board code runs on the single thread. set_filesys_unit_1 refuses everything but a hard file on the UAE controller (host directories, archives, CDs, tapes and other controllers have no provider in the profile), filesys_init_storeinfo no longer asks for an extended trap (its body only reads 68k registers), the resident id string carries no build date of the host, exter_int_helper drains native2amiga_pending under P6_NATIVE2AMIGA, two unbounded _stprintf into pointers become snprintf, the shell-execution code uses snprintf and my_strdup and the RDB file system version reader a local p6_atol (the Waterbox guest imports from libc only what ports/waterbox/imports.json lists), and the save/restore bodies (host paths, savestate.cpp helpers the profile does not build) wait for T29c under SAVESTATE. pt_rdsk, which parses what a disk says about itself, refuses an RDB block size that is not a power of two between 256 and FILESYS_MAX_BLOCKSIZE (it sized an xmalloc), ends a chain of FSHD blocks after 1024 (nothing in the disk ended a loop) and widens the block offsets to 64 bits.

patches.title: The trap area installs the filesystem boot code and keeps no host memory protection
patches.reason: T29a: rtarea_init copies the filesystem boot ROM (filesys_install_code) under FILESYS, which stays excluded as a feature; it runs under P6_FILESYS, and only when the session mounts a hard file (devices.cpp). boot_rom_copy (uaeboard 3) no longer names protect_roms, which the profile does not build, and uae_int_requested stays defined by ports/portable/atomic.cpp (the portable probes link it without the engine).

patches.title: The UAEFS board, the UAE boot ROM and the trap-area RAM exist when a hard file is mounted
patches.reason: T29a: PUAE5 mounts a hard file through the UAE controller (uae0): a Zorro II board of 64 KiB whose DiagArea runs filesys_diagentry, and the boot ROM at $F00000. 0053 excluded all of it for the A500; it comes back under P6_FILESYS (FILESYS stays excluded as a feature). need_uae_boot_rom is upstream's again: check_boot_rom answers 0 unless some condition holds, and the only one that can hold in the profile is a mounted unit of the UAE controller (nr_directory_units counts every mount configuration of that controller), so a machine without a hard file is the one that was built before. uaeboard_alloc_ram and uaeboard_map_ram return: the filesystem keeps its shared records in the board.

patches.title: The device lifecycle starts, resets and frees the trap area, uaehf.device and the UAEFS board when a hard file is mounted
patches.reason: T29a: virtualdevice_init, devices_reset and virtualdevice_free ran the FILESYS parts behind a feature that is excluded. They run now behind P6_FILESYS and a runtime test (a mount configuration exists), so a session without a hard file creates no trap area and no queue and resets nothing of it; with one, the order is upstream's: rtarea_setup, rtarea_init, uaeres_install, hardfile_install, expansion_init, filesys_install, and the EXTER queue (native2amiga_install, which main.cpp calls under AUTOCONFIG) is allocated and given back with the image.

patches.title: A-line traps, the autoconfig window and the boot ROM bank are reachable while a hard file is mounted
patches.reason: T29a: the CPU treats an A-line opcode as a trap call only inside the trap area (in_rtarea: uae_boot_rom_type is 0 without a hard file, so every other session keeps the illegal-instruction exception), the memory map puts the boot ROM bank at rtarea_base through need_uae_boot_rom (0 without a hard file), and the autoconfig window and its reset are taken as for a Fast RAM board when a hard file is mounted.
